children: Many of the major streaming stocks have lost significant ground since January, with Paramount Skydance
, Netflix
, Versant
, and Comcast
down over 20% year-to-date.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and
if now was the time to buy streaming stocks and, if so, which ones?

: Investors' enthusiasm around streaming is clearly past its peak, and rightfully so. They have recognized that streaming is not a new growth story but a simple shift in the type of TV consumption and the technology that delivers it.
For legacy media companies like Disney
and Comcast
, this renders streaming a necessary new income stream, offsetting linear TV declines. For pure players like Netflix
or Amazon's

Prime Video, it created an opportunity to capture shares in the broader entertainment realm. Streaming has reached a rather saturated steady state, where growth is harder to come by and competition is fierce.
After skepticism around Netflix

a year ago, I am turning more bullish now that the stock trades 33% lower. These valuation levels around 20x earnings more realistically represent the maturing state and slowing growth of the industry.
I have long had an even more bullish stance on Disney
and Comcast

. Neither, however, are to be seen as streaming stocks. Real-life experiences are far more profitable ways of monetizing their IP, and both companies have announced new theme parks for the early 2030s.
Daniel Jones: Even though it is not a pure play in the streaming space, my favorite streaming company has got to be The Walt Disney Company
One of the reasons why I like Disney

from a streaming perspective is because of its diversification. You're not buying into a single streaming platform. You're buying into three of them: Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN. And all of them are significant in size and varied in terms of content. Plus, management continues to make major investments and see meaningful traction when it comes to these platforms.

Management has spoken of its efforts to connect Disney's services into a single ecosystem, and this specifically involves Disney+. For instance, the company hopes to turn it into a comprehensive membership ecosystem that integrates high-value, always-on benefits with its storytelling. Recently, the company allowed Hulu Standalone and Bundle subscribers to link profiles, watch history, and manage subscriptions on Disney+, and even added social clips to Disney+ Verts.

Disney also entered into a major deal with TikTok that will bring creators to the forefront of the platform by using a curated feed of fan-created content featuring its characters and stories. As for ESPN, the company has unlocked a selection of content on Disney+ domestically. That started in 2024 but has been expanding globally.

This all tells a story of a business that is integrating assets in a way that creates a flywheel effect while facilitating product stickiness that makes customer churn less likely over the long run. This is a phenomenal strategy if you ask me and something that other streaming platforms largely lack.
The benefit to investing in Disney

as a streaming play is that you get more than just streaming. And the business as a whole seems to be doing quite nicely. For the first nine months of 2026, revenue ended up being 6.2% higher than the year before. And while net income was down due to changes in taxes, adjusted operating cash flow ended up rising 6.7%. So clearly, the company is doing well at the moment.
(Daniel Jones runs the investment newsletter Crude Value Insights.)
